study.question: Can raw user/context and event-aligned historical actions condition field-specific event selection more effectively than perturbing the target query with a pooled history state?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: g1-r0004-field_d1_q0 reaches click AUC 0.6571361136 versus 0.6552234734 for tied-field Q0 and 0.6555440824 for DIN, but adding history-derived query feedback yields 0.6546278483. At Q0 the field-weight effect is +0.0019126402; at Q1 it is -0.0020700290, interaction -0.0039826692. These are one-seed controlled observations, not repeated mechanism support. Code shows that current context and historical actions reach prediction/readout, while selection scores see target/item fields only. Hypothesis: preserving target identity and modulating scorer hidden channels with raw context and visible per-event feedback provides useful selection conditioning without the pooled-feedback bottleneck. Alternative explanations include target distortion, optimizer dynamics and initialization. Cross-trajectory audit: round0 exchange cells all lost to DIN; round1 mass restored quality but peaked at 0.6533304082; round2 raw-value rescue peaked at 0.6514672042 and did not recover its mass parent; round3 native Q/W combined 0.6533441923 lost to no-feedback 0.6557366273; round4 field-addressable Q0 is promising but feedback is antagonistic. None establishes that all unified designs fail or that one information bottleneck is proven.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary DIN text lines250-283 supports target-conditioned unnormalized local activation. Retain that ingredient with original-coordinate field values; introduce context/action modulation before field-specific output scores. Adapted four-task baseline is not an exact DIN reproduction.

Pinned benchmark forward/ESTBlocks use projected sequence tokens, cross-attention and feature-specific FFNs. Inherit only the previous locally implemented field-addressable retrieval comparison; new design uses bounded hidden-channel modulation, no projected sequence token update or heterogeneous token FFN. Original EST paper not audited; no originality claim.

Pinned forward uses action-mask task hubs and iterative aggregation/broadcast; BroadcastGatedUnit applies hub-derived affine modulation to token states. Here transform raw user/context and individual historical action embeddings into bounded multiplicative gates on a local activation scorer, retain target and raw values, and ablate both routes factorially. No task hubs, task-mask aggregation, token broadcast stack, or mask-free attention adopted. Original paper text unavailable through registry; nearest-work novelty remains unverified.

Two reads averaged; first-read field interaction and two side vectors retained as head inputs, with no query feedback

study.proposed_difference: Let h_t=DiceMLP([q,k_t,q-k_t,q*k_t]), c=tanh(Wc*context), a_t=tanh(Wa*historical_action_t). First read uses field_scores(h_t); second uses field_scores(h_t*(1+0.5*C*c)*(1+0.5*A*a_t)), with C,A in {0,1}; both reads keep q=target. Field-specific sums use original masked values, without softmax. All four heads additionally receive c and masked_mean(a_t) in every cell, keeping each projection active even when its retrieval edge is disabled. All four standalone modules have identical source except CONFIG; gates are shared across value-field output rows but can change their scores differently. Each gate factor lies in (0.5,1.5); this bounds modulation, not accumulated unnormalized interest magnitude. This is a coherent information-placement mechanism test, not a novel-method priority claim.
predictions: Primary: each enabled route should improve full-population validation click AUC against its matched off-edge control. Joint complementarity requires positive factorial interaction AND joint AUC exceeding both singles. Improvement over incumbent is a separate selection criterion.

Report all four task AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean separately, parameters, allocated GPU/wall seconds, examples, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95 batch latency from host receipts. Keep one-pass matched-recipe mechanism comparisons distinct from measured quality-cost comparisons.

Host-provided predefined empty, 1-16,17-64,>64 history slices are diagnostic; report N/positive/negative counts, label small slices insufficient and treat slice directions as exploratory. No unseen frequency/hour/composition diagnostics are asserted unless available under the existing host interface. No fabricated task-specific or bootstrap results.

A=1 has no direct retrieval effect on an all-masked history with fixed weights; C may still affect heads through its retained side path in every cell. Across independently trained cells empty-history differences need not be zero. Padding-ID changes under fixed masks must not change predictions for either mode; actual host tests required.
falsifiers: Nonpositive C simple effects fail the context-selection benefit prediction for this implementation; nonpositive A simple effects fail the historical-action-selection benefit prediction.
Joint cell failing to exceed both single-route controls, or I<=0, fails joint complementarity even if one cell beats DIN.
If off-edge capacity control matches or exceeds enabled cells, new routing is unsupported; historical-incumbent improvement alone cannot identify routing.

Finite outputs/gradients, correct four [B,1] probabilities, current-target-action exclusion, invalid-history-ID invariance and empty-history safety are host prerequisites. Failure invalidates the attempted cell and remains charged; do not reinterpret an execution failure as scientific counterevidence.
Loss of a positive direction across subsequent paired seeds or failure of a cost-matched/replacement control downgrades support; a single failing implementation does not refute the general mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Additional dense projection/readout capacity or changed initialization relative to the incumbent; controlled by the new off-edge cell, only partially by old trials.
Added gradient paths, gate-induced reparameterization or signed-weight scale/calibration rather than semantically better event selection.
Rare feedback estimation and mismatch between auxiliary category/brand labels and advertisement-specific outcomes.
One-seed randomness, temporal validation adaptation and repeated model selection; no significance or independent replication claim.
Dice includes zero-padded positions in batch statistics despite pre-masking; padding IDs are erased, but mask-length and batch-composition sensitivity remains inherited.
Bounded gates may underfit or optimize slowly under the frozen one-epoch recipe; no recipe changes or rescaled learning rates are allowed.
Offline feedback maturity, whole-window filtering/vocabularies and static publisher snapshots limit point-in-time transfer.
No position/time features or sequence-order sensitivity introduced; this tests selective history aggregation, not temporal order modeling.
